notes: Summary: Heliotrope is a UK-based legaltech platform (case management + e-discovery) looking to replace an on-prem vector index with a managed solution that meets strict EU/UK residency and low-latency SLAs.
Scale: initial index ~20M documents (legal briefs + filings). Expected growth to 80M+ over 18 months. High-cardinality metadata (case ids, dates) for rerankers.
Performance targets: target tail latency p99 < 120ms for typical queries (<512 tokens). Throughput target during working hours ~3k qps across UK/EU; burst to 6k qps.
Cost sensitivity: target cost-per-query (embedding+rerank) < $0.002 for steady-state; willing to trade slight latency uplift for 30% cost savings via quantized models and batching.
Routing/failover: require multi-region routing with primary UK (eu-west-2) and failover to Frankfurt (eu-central-1). Need cross-region warm caches or fast cold-start behavior.
Security: must support SSO (SAML), KMS-managed keys, audit logs retained 2 years, vendor SOC2/ISO evidence required. Legal requested data residency contract language (see drive doc).

Model preferences: prefer open/quantized transformer weights for reranking; want ability to fall back to cheaper model variant on capacity constraints; interested in Redwood Optimize recommendations for quantization profiles.
POC scope discussed: index ingestion pipeline (30k docs/hr), embedding throughput test (batch vs streaming), rerank latency measurements, cost sim with real query mix.
Notes from 2025-01-15 call (ff_2025_01_15_3287): 'Latency is make-or-break — if search is slower than legacy ES we won't move. Also legal will push for UK data residency enforcement in contract.'
2025-01-29: SE demo of routing rules and canary rollouts. Confirmed can pin model versions and set fallback to smaller quantized reranker. SE action: provide config + expected cost spreadsheet.

Procurement: procurement team looped in (thread-20250203-procurement). CFO requested 3-year reserved vs flexible pricing comparison — provided high-level deck (drive link) but need granular ARR estimate.
Technical concerns raised: indexing time for full rebuild (80M docs) and how shard/replica strategy maps to dedicated pools; need clear guidance on autoscaling policies and warm-up times.

Competitive signals: they trialed Pinecone for vector infra but hit EU residency limits and higher-than-expected cost at scale; also evaluated Elastic vectors but had poor reranking latency with their pipeline.
Decision drivers: residency + predictable tail latency + transparent cost control (batching/caching knobs) + strong operational telemetry. Redwood's dedicated + private options are top of shortlist.
Short-term ask: detailed POC technical plan and estimated cost-per-query for the defined 20M doc workload; timeline for legal to review residency clause (legal lead: Emma Hart).
Longer-term: plan for regional expansion (APAC) in year 2 if EU/UK rollout succeeds — want multi-region replication model and disaster recovery playbook.
Contact rhythm: weekly syncs on Thursdays; SE office hours Tuesdays for ingest / index tuning.
AE notes: keep procurement happy with clear reserved vs on-demand numbers; escalate legal residency template to Sales Ops if legal stalls >3 weeks.
